japanese:
予言者は云った・・・







『そなたたち人間が、迷い、

　世の秩序が土くれのごとく

　風に舞うとき・・・

　我らを創りし主は、

　そなたたちに最後の試練を

　与えるだろう。



　それは、高きを目指すこと

　それは、滴る血を拭うこと

　それは、恐怖を捨てること

　それは、後戻りしないこと

　総ては摩天楼より生まれ、

　摩天楼に帰するのだ・・・



　そなたに力があるのならば

　摩天楼に挑むがよい。



　そなたに知恵があるのなら

　摩天楼に問うがよい。　　



　そなたに欲望があるのなら

　摩天楼を望むがよい。　　



　我が主は、必ずや

　そなたたちの前に現れる。

　摩天楼をその手にした者の

　前に・・・』







眼前にそびえ立つその塔が

摩天楼なのか・・・

終わりなき頂上を目指し、

今日も一人の男が塔に挑み

その審判を受ける・・・



その手に掴むは、

神の力か、それとも死か。

その心に刻むは、

勇気か、それとも絶望か。
english:
From the words of the prophet 







"When you humans lose your way 

 when the world's balance is thrown about

 like gravel in the wind 

 Then the Lord who built us 

 shall put you 

 to the final test. 



 You shall aim for the summit; 

 You shall wipe the blood that has been spilled; 

 You shall abandon fear; 

 You shall never turn back. 

 All that was born from the Wolkenkratzer, 

 shall return to the Wolkenkratzer. 



 If you have the strength 

 then defy the Wolkenkratzer. 



 If you have the wits, 

 then question the Wolkenkratzer. 



 If you have the ambition, 

 then demand from the Wolkenkratzer. 



 Mark our words, as we promise 

 that, in front of the one 

  who seizes the Wolkenkratzer 

 our Lord shall reveal Himself."







 This towering building... 

 Could it be that Wolkenkratzer? 

 Today, again, someone has arrived before it 

 to defy its ever-extending heights 

 and face its judgement. 



 What will they gain from it? 

 The power of a god, or their own death?

 What will be left engraved in their heart? 

 Bravery, or despair?

japanese: これから、その若者の物語をはじめよう・・・・
english: The story of this young fellow now begins...

japanese: そして、ここに「勇者」になることを夢みて旅立つ若者がいた。
english: A young man set out on a journey, in the hopes of becoming a hero of tales.

japanese: たとえ、その結末が死であったとしても
english: Even if death were the only thing awaiting them

japanese: しかし、人々は時間をかけてでも夢を追いかける。
english: People still poured their lives into the pursuit of such dreams.

japanese: 時の流れは止まらない、人の命は時間と言う火で消費される。
english: The course of time cannot be stopped; it erases, inescapably, the lives of men.

japanese: 下記くけこぉそせすしさ！
ヴォルケンクラッツァー
何処からか声が聞こえた。
真の頂上へ挑むが良い。
english: And try to reach its true summit.

japanese: 摩天楼が揺れているようだ。
english: The Wolkenkratzer seems to be shaking.

japanese: 風がどこからともなく吹いてくる
english: A wind is blowing, but it is impossible to tell where it is coming from.

japanese: 清らかな波動が伝わって来る。
english: You can sense a pleasant vibration.

japanese: まわりの雑草が枯れ果てている。
english: The grass around here is dried up.
It's so hot.\n\nHot enough to kill.

japanese: 何かが素早く移動しているようだ
english: Something seems to be moving quickly.

japanese: 異国の雰囲気が漂っている。
english: You can sense an unusual fragrance, as if from a foreign land.

japanese: かわいた尻尾がおちている。
english: There is a dried-up tail on the floor.

japanese: 何かを唱えているようだ。
english: The musical tones of a sort of chant can be heard.

japanese: ひからびた男の死体が転がっている。
english: A man's corpse, dried to a husk, lies on the floor.

japanese: 穴のあいたものが沢山落ちている
english: The floor is littered with holed, broken things.

japanese: 腹にひびく吠え声が聞こえる。
すえた匂いがする。それに寒い。
english: There is a sour smell. And it's cold.

japanese: ひからびた死骸がころがっている
english: Dried up bones lie scattered on the floor.

japanese: 石像を砕いたような小石が多い。
english: There are many small rocks, as if a statue had been shattered.
Something bad seems to be on the verge of happening.

japanese: 急激に熱くなった。\n\n摩天楼が揺れているようだ。
english: It's suddenly becoming very hot.\n\nThe Wolkenkratzer seems to be trembling.

japanese: 風がどこからともなく吹いている
english: A wind is blowing, but it is impossible to tell where it is coming from.

japanese: 熱い・・・汗が出てくる。
english: It's so hot... The sweat is unbearable.

japanese: 何か巨大な物が移動しているようだ。
english: Something vast is moving; you can feel it.
You can hear the beating of wings.

japanese: 大きな硬い物を引きずった跡がある。
english: There are traces of a big, solid thing being dragged.

japanese: 金属のぶつかりあう音が聞こえる
暑い。\n\n空気も乾燥している。
english: It's hot.\n\nThe air is drying up.

japanese: 背筋が寒くなる。\n\nゾクゾクする。
english: A chill runs down your spine.

japanese: 妙な声が聞こえる。\n\n悪臭も漂っている。
english: Strange voices can be heard.\n\nA strong smell floats in the air.

japanese: 空気がじめじめしている。
english: The air is saturated with humidity.
It's so cold.\n\nYour body is shaking.

japanese: 植物が枯れている。\n\n土もひからびている。
空気がじめじめしている。\n\n雑草が腐っている。
english: The air is saturated with humidity.\n\nThe vegetation is rotting.

japanese: すえた匂いがする。それに暑い。
english: It smells bad. And it's hot.

japanese: 空気が湿っている。\n\n泥の匂いもする。
english: The air is humid.\n\nIt smells of mud.

japanese: すえた匂いがする。\n\n虫の死骸も多い。
english: There is a sour smell.\n\nInsect carcasses are everywhere.

japanese: 土と朽ち木の匂いがする。
english: It smells of dirt and decayed wood.

japanese: こんな場所に女性がいるのか？
english: Could there be a woman in a place like this?

japanese: 邪悪な念が伝わってくる。
english: A vile intent. So intense you can feel it.

japanese: 急激に寒くなった。\n\n摩天楼が揺れているようだ。
english: The temperature suddenly dropped.\n\nThe Wolkenkratzer seems to be shaking.

japanese: 気温が高くなってきた。\n\n獣臭もする。
english: The temperature rose.\n\nThere is the smell of a beast in the air.

japanese: 本当に塔から逃げますか？
english: Do you really wish to flee the tower?

japanese: ５０階まで上がり『勇者の証』を手に入れ世界を導くが良い。
english: Climb the 50 floors, bring back the Hero's Emblem, and you shall become the ruler of the world.

japanese: まずは、西の扉を開きドラゴンを倒すが良い。
english: You should first open the Western door and kill the dragon there.
There is nothing left for you to learn.\n\n
You lost one point of defense.\n\n
You lost one point of attack.\n\n
You lost one point of strength.\n\n

japanese: 塔の中で死んだらそのチャレンジは回数に含まれないのよ。
english: If you die in the tower, no record will be kept.

japanese: 摩天楼の神はその人が何回チャレンジしたかちゃんと記録しているのよ。
english: The number of times somebody has challenged the Wolkenkratzer is recorded.

japanese: キャンプ中に中断してもそこから再開できるわよ。でもそれは１回だけ。死んだら街からよ。
english: You can save and quit at the camp, to continue later, but only once. Die, and you're sent back to town.

japanese: 塔の中には制限時間があるらしいの。それを越えると神の声が聞こえるんですって。
english: There appears to be a time-limit in the tower. Those who exceed it can hear God's voice.

japanese: 奥義の巻物って知ってる？　それを使うと必殺技を覚えられるんですって。
english: Do you know about the secret technique scrolls? It is said you can use them to learn special tricks.

japanese: アイテムは一度使ってみないとなんだか判らないの。
english: You'll never know what an item does until you try it.

japanese: 塔の中で上がった能力は塔から出ると元に戻っちゃうの。でも武器の威力はそのままなのよ。
english: The skills you learn in the tower are forgotten when you return to town. But you don't lose your weapons.

japanese: 塔に関する噂なら街で沢山聞けるわよ。
english: Tons of rumors about the tower can be heard in town.

japanese: あなたも塔にチャレンジ？
english: So you're going to challenge the tower too?

japanese: 摩天楼を囲む街にようこそ！
english: Welcome to the town at the base of the Wolkenkratzer!

japanese:
現在の状態を保存します。

宜しいですか？
english:
This will save your current state.

Do you wish to proceed?

japanese: データを保存しています。\n\nカードを抜いたり電源を切ったりしないで下さい。
english:
Data is being saved.

Please don't cut the power or remove the memory card.

japanese: アイテムを選択してください。\n\n

english: What do you wish to do?\n\n

japanese:
持ち物が一杯です。

持ち物を捨てて下さい。
english:
Your inventory is full.

Please drop something.

japanese: 残りアイテムを破棄しますか？\n\n
english: Do you wish to abandon the rest of the items?\n\n

japanese: アイテムを破棄しました。\n\n
english: The rest of the items are gone.\n\n

japanese: タイプを選択して下さい。\n\n
ボタンを押せば起きます。\n\n
english: Press a button to wake up.\n\n

japanese:
冒険を中断します。

宜しいですか？
english:
This will interrupt your adventure.

Do you wish to proceed?

japanese: データを保存しています。\n\nカードを抜いたり電源を切ったりしないで下さい。
english: Data is being saved.\n\nPlease don't cut the power or remove the memory card.

japanese:
保存出来ました。

ゲームを中断します。
english:
Data has been saved.

The game will end now.

japanese: レベルアップしました。\n\n

english: Your hit points rose by XX.

japanese: 僕キーガン。僕塔に登るのが夢なんだ。だから一生懸命剣の技を勉強してるんだよ。
english: The name is Keegan. Climbing the tower is my dream. This is why I have dedicated my life to the art of the sword.

japanese: 基本は上段斬り、中段斬り、下段斬り、防御、この４つさ。
english: The basics are upper slashes, middle slashes, lower slashes and defense. Those four.

japanese: すぐ離れたがるモンスターには素早く間合いを詰める技を使うと便利だよ。
english: Against monsters that back off the moment you approach, a technique that closes the gap fast comes in handy.

japanese: 剣技は突きと斬りに分けられるんだ。突きは点の攻撃、斬りは線の攻撃が出来るんだ。
english: We divide sword techniques into two categories: thrusts and slashes. Thrusts aim to pierce a point, while slashes are cutting attacks.

japanese: 突きの基本は斬りと一緒で上段、中段、下段だよ。
english: The basics of thrusting are the same as for slashing: upper strokes, middle strokes and lower strokes.

japanese: 垂直斬りっていうのは斬りの中では一番威力があってその名の通り垂直に振り下ろす技だよ。
english: The vertical slash is the most powerful of the slashing techniques. Just like the name says: you slash straight down.

japanese: カブト割りっていうのはジャンプして上から剣を振り下ろす技なんだ。
english: During a skull splitter, you bring down your sword as you jump.

japanese: 回転斬りっていうのは自分がコマみたいに回ってどの方向にも対応できる技だよ。
english: In a whirlwind, the swordfighter spins in place, striking in every direction.

japanese: 払い斬りっていうのは左下から右上に剣を払うように振る技だよ。
english: The sweep is a slashing technique during which the sword sweeps an area from the bottom left to the top right.

japanese: ドラゴンソードを装備してＤアタックすれば、ドラゴンに凄いダメージを与えられるんだ。
english: If you perform a Dragonslayer while equipped with the Dragon Sword, you'll inflict tremendous damage to dragons.

japanese: Ｘ斬りっていうのは払い斬りの後１回転して左上から右下に剣を振り下ろす技だよ。
english: A cross slash involves performing a second sweep after a sword sweep, swinging around from the top left to the bottom right.

japanese: 前転斬りっていうのは前宙しながら剣を振る技だよ。離れた所にいるモンスターに届くんだ。
english: In a somersault slash, the swordfighter jumps forward with sword extended. It is effective to reach monsters that are at a distance.

japanese: 乱れ突きって言うのは上段突き、中段突き、下段突きを連続して繰り出す技だよ。
english: The wild thrusts consist of chaining multiple high, middle and low thrusts in quick succession.

japanese: 三段払いっていうのは前方に移動してコマみたいに回転しながら３回払い斬りする技だよ。
english: During the three sweeps combo, the swordfighter moves forward, spinning while sweeping three times.

japanese: 接近突きっていうのは敵に詰め寄って中段突きをする技で、隙が大きいんだ。
english: The lunge is a technique that lets you close in on a foe thanks to a middle thrust, but it leaves you open.

japanese: 対空払いっていうのは垂直にジャンプしながら払い斬りをする技だよ。
english: To perform an anti-air sweep, the fighter jumps up and sweeps while in the air.

japanese: 側転斬りっていうのは前転斬りより高くジャンプするから飛んでるモンスターも斬れるんだ。
english: The hurricane slash is a somersault slash done with more height. You can cut flying monsters that way.

japanese: Ｄフライっていうのは剣を頭の上に構えて回転しながら垂直にジャンプする技だよ。
english: In a dragonfly, you jump up with the sword held over the head, spinning it.

japanese: 垂直割りっていうのは垂直にジャンプして剣を振り下ろす技で一番威力のある技なんだ。
english: The vertical split is the most powerful technique, jumping straight up and bringing the sword down.

japanese: 技っていっていいのか解らないけど、ジャンプっていうのがあるんだ。なんなんだろう？
english: Whether it is worth calling it a technique or not, the jump is important. You can probably guess what it involves.

japanese: あんなに説明してあげたのにまだ制覇してないの？
english: I gave you all those careful instructions and you still haven't mastered it?

japanese: 人によって技の好みが違うみたいだけどあなたは何が好き？
english: Everybody has their own taste, so what are your favorite techniques?

japanese: 一つの技におぼれないっていうのはセオリーだよ。技は沢山覚えないとね。
english: You can't rely on just one technique. You gotta learn a lot of them.

japanese: モンスターごとに技を使い分けられればいいんだけど、覚えてないとどうしようもないよね。
english: It's good practice to use specific techniques against given monsters, but you still gotta learn which ones first.

japanese: 最初に覚えた技がジャンプだったら大変だね。
english: It would be a real hassle if the first technique you learned was "Jump."

japanese: 防御してモンスターの攻撃を防いだら斬る。こいつが基本だがタイミングが命だぜ。
english: Defend first, then strike the monster after you parried its attack. That may sound obvious, but mastering its timing is of the essence.

japanese: 初めのうちは毒を吐く奴が多い。だから盾で防御が肝心だ。
english: You'll face lots of poison spitting foes at first. That's where protecting yourself behind a shield is vital.

japanese: 怪我したくねぇんならモンスターの攻撃の間合いを見切るんだな。
english: If you don't wanna get hurt, you gotta be able to estimate a monster's reach at a glance.

japanese: 虫のモンスターは基本的に動きが速い奴が多いんだ。パニックになったら負けるぜ。
english: The insect monsters are basically fast moving jerks. Panic, and you're dead.

japanese: 西の扉すら制覇してないひよっ子に話す事はねえな。
english: I have really nothing to say to a big baby who hasn't even cleared the West Portal.

japanese: フン、やっと中央の扉に行けるようになったのか。
english: Oh, finally, you have what it takes to get through the Center Portal.

japanese: 虫や草は火に弱い。こんなのは常識だぜ。
english: Insects, plants: they hate fire. That's common sense.

japanese: ここを攻略するコツはタイミングよく街に帰る事だな。
english: The key to success is to learn the right time to get back to town.

japanese: 俺は中央の扉の３５階まで登った事があるぜ。
english: I have reached the 35th floor of the Center Portal. Yep.

japanese: 防御の重要さも解らない奴に摩天楼に挑む資格なんかねぇな。
english: Why bother defying the Wolkenkratzer if you don't even understand why defense matters?

japanese: 扉の前で耳をすましても何がいるか判らねぇ時には、周りを調べてみな。少しはヒントになるぜ。
english: If you can't tell what's coming by listening at the door, try paying attention to your surroundings. It should tell you something.

japanese: ちったぁマシになってきたみたいだな。
english: Oh, seems like you're not as bad as you were before. Slightly.

japanese: 羽音と凄まじい振動を感じたら、そこにいるのはドラゴンだ。せいぜい気を付けるこったな。
english: If you hear wings flapping and feel a crazy tremor, you can bet there is a dragon out there. Better be careful with that.

japanese: ゴーレムは額には真理が詰まってる。だから狙うなら頭だな。
english: A golem's whole life is in its forehead. Aim for the head.

japanese: 逆鱗って知ってるか？\n\nドラゴンの一番頭に近い鱗の事なんだってよ。
english: The gap in the armor.\n\nThat's what the scale closest to a dragon's head is called.

japanese: 俺はまだ会ったこたぁねぇんだけどよ、上の方にはえれぇ強ぇ異国の剣士がいるらしいぜ。
english: Never met him, but I heard about some foreign knight that's supposed to be a helluva badass at the top of the tower.

japanese: モンスターにも弱点ってモンがあるんだ。それを覚えりゃ素早く倒せるようになるだろうよ。
english: Monsters have weak points. Spot them, and you'll dispatch them in no time.

japanese: ジャイアントの左手・・・。思い出すだけで鳥肌がたってくるぜ。
english: The left hand of a giant... I got the chills just thinking back about it.

japanese: でかい奴を相手にするときゃ懐にもぐりこんじまやぁ意外と楽に戦えるぜ。
english: When facing some gargantuan guys, it's surprisingly effective to get in very close.

japanese: 俺が言ってるのは３５階までの事だ。それより上で俺の言った事と違っても責任もてねぇぞ。
english: I can only speak of what happens up to the 35th floor. After that point, don't blame me if what I told you doesn't apply anymore.

japanese: 摩天楼の中で死んだ奴は、何処かで新たな生を受けるって話だぜ。
english: It's said the people that die in the Wolkenkratzer start a new life elsewhere.

japanese: モンスターどもは大体出てくるエリアが決まってんだ。嫌な奴がいたらとっとと抜けるんだな。
english: Monsters generally dwell in specific areas. You should be able to avoid the ones you really don't like.

japanese: 西の扉のドラゴンは、本物のドラゴンとはちょっと違う。本物はもっと強いぜ。
english: The West Portal dragon ain't no real dragon. True ones are way stronger.

japanese: 服を着たガイコツ野郎と戦う時は間合いを詰めた方がいいぜ。
english: You better close the gap when fighting that robed skeleton.

japanese: さすがの俺も熊があんな攻撃をしてくるとは思わなかったぜ。
english: Well, I damn well would never have imagined a bear could pull that attack.

japanese: 俺はマギー。\n\nアイテムの事なら任せとけ。
english: I'm Maggy.\n\nIf you need to know something about items, just ask me.

japanese: シールドに鏡の粉でメッキをすれば毒を受けなくなるぞ。
english: If you coat a shield with mirror powder, you won't have to worry about getting poisoned anymore.

japanese: 剣や鎧は粉をふりかけることで強くも弱くもなるぞ。
english: Spraying powders over armors and weapons can have either a good or a bad effect.

japanese: 剣や鎧は粉９個まで強くなるぞ。
english: You can spray up to nine powders on one weapon or piece of armor.

japanese: アイテム探しに熱を上げるのもいいが時間には気を付けろよ。
english: It's good practice to focus on gathering items, but be careful with the time spent.

japanese: フレアシールドは火の魔法を無効にするんだ。
english: The flare shield neutralizes fire magic.

japanese: アイスシールドは氷の魔法を無効にするんだ。
english: The ice shield neutralizes ice magic.

japanese: エレキシールドは雷の魔法を無効にするんだ。
english: The shock shield neutralizes lightning magic.

japanese: オールシールドはすべての魔法を無効にするんだ。
english: The all shield neutralizes all magic.

japanese: ドラゴンにはガルブレイズよりドラゴンソードの方がよく効くぞ。
english: The dragon sword is more effective against dragons than the Galblaze.

japanese: 盾にメッキをしてあれば毒攻撃は防げるが、毒薬を飲んだ場合は別だ。忘れるな。
english: A coated shield can protect you from poison attacks, but not from drinking poison. Don't forget that.

japanese: この前、錆びた剣と溶けた鎧が欲しいって奴がいたな。一体何に使うんだか。
english: I remember some fellow who was interested in rusted swords and melted armor. I really wonder what he wanted to do with those.

japanese: 何の薬か判らない時、戦闘中使うのは無謀ってもんだ。
english: It's ill-advised to use a pill during a fight when you don't know its effects.

japanese: 戦士の家系なら巻物は大事にしろよ。
english: If you are of warrior lineage, then cherish the scrolls!

japanese: 攻撃に使える巻物は魔法と同じでフレア、アイス、エレキの３つだが、それぞれレベルがあるぞ。
english: The offensive scrolls come in flare, ice and shock varieties, just like magic, but with different levels.

japanese: 粉や薬にはそれぞれ相反するものがある。例えば体力回復薬と劇薬だ。
english: Powders and pills have opposites. For every great medicine there's an equally great poison.

japanese: 魔法回復薬に相反するのは混乱の薬だ。
english: The opposite of a pill of restoring magic is a pill of confusion.

japanese: 毒薬に相反するのは読んだ通り解毒薬だ。
english: The opposite of a pill of poison is, as expected, a pill of antidote.

japanese: 防御ＵＰ粉に相反するのは酸の粉だ。
english: The opposite of def. up powder is an acid powder.

japanese: 攻撃ＵＰ粉に相反するのは錆の粉だ。
english: The opposite of an atk. up powder is a rust powder.

japanese: 俺さぁ、ボンっていうんだけどさぁ、ステータス関係なら割と詳しいんだよねぇ。
english: Me? Okay, let's say the name is Bom. Well, you're not gonna want to miss what I can tell you about status and such...

japanese: モンスターから毒攻撃を受けるとさぁ、腕に力が入らなくなるんだよねぇ。
english: Let's say you get poisoned by a monster. Well, you're not gonna be able to hit as hard anymore...

japanese: いくらレベルが上がってもさぁ、防御力は変わらないんだよねぇ。まぁ鎧次第って事かなぁ。
english: Let's say you level up more and more. Well, you're not gonna raise defense that way. That's because defense only comes from armor, not level.

japanese: 毒を受けたまま登ると結構危ないからさぁ、解毒薬を飲むか街に戻るかした方がいいよぉ。
english: Let's say you are poisoned, and you keep climbing the tower. Well, you're not gonna last long, you wanna get back to town to drink an antidote, I tell ya.

japanese: 人間の能力ってさぁ、腕力と知力と素早さの３つがあるんだよねぇ
english: Let's say there are three statistics. Well, don't forget their names: strength, intelligence and speed.

japanese: どんなに体がおっきくてもさぁ、腕力が低けりゃぁただの木偶の坊なんだよねぇ。
english: Let's say you got that big, bulky body. Well, you're not gonna do much damage if you ain't got the strength to go with it.

japanese: 素早さの高い人ってさぁ、時間をあまり使わないんだよねぇ。当然だけどさぁ、大事だよぉ。
english: Let's say you are of the speedy kind. Well, you're not gonna waste as much time as others. Yeah, well it may be obvious, but it is still true.

japanese: 知力が高いとさぁ、魔法の効きがいいんだよねぇ。まぁ、俺には関係無いけどねぇ。
english: Let's say you're smart. Well, you're gonna get more out of magic. Not me.

japanese: 攻撃力ってさぁ、腕力と武器の威力で決まるんだよねぇ。
english: Let's say you want to deal real damage. Well, you're gonna need both strength and the weapon to go with it.

japanese: レベルアップだけに頼ってるとさぁ、多分きついよぉ。やっぱり薬を使わないとねぇ。
english: Let's say you only care about leveling up. That's still gonna be tough. You're gonna need potions.

japanese: 家系によってさぁ、能力の上がり方に差があるんだよねぇ。
english: Let's say that depending on your lineage, you're gonna want to raise your stats differently.

japanese: 実はさぁ、俺家系にもちょっと詳しいんだよねぇ。
english: Well, it happens that I'm a bit versed in the various trades, if you wanna hear.

japanese: 腕力が一番上がるのは当然戦士だよねぇ。後は騎士、レンジャー、魔法使いの順なんだよねぇ。
english: Let's say strength matters the most to fighters, then knights, rangers and magic users, in that order.

japanese: 体力が一番上がるのは当然戦士だよねぇ。後は騎士、レンジャー、魔法使いの順なんだよねぇ。
english: Let's say hit points matter the most to fighters, then knights, rangers and magic users, in that order.

japanese: 知力が一番上がるのは当然魔法使いだよねぇ。後はレンジャー、騎士、戦士の順なんだよねぇ。
english: Let's say intelligence matters the most to magic users, then rangers, knights and fighters, in that order.

japanese: 魔法力が一番上がるのは当然魔法使いだよねぇ。後はレンジャー、騎士、戦士の順なんだよねぇ。
english: Let's say magic points matter the most to magic users, then rangers, knights and fighters, in that order.

japanese: 素早さっていえばさぁ、やっぱりレンジャーだよねぇ。
english: Let's say that when it comes to speed, you wanna be a ranger.

japanese: こんなしゃべり方してるんだけどさぁ、俺あんたの事尊敬してるんだよねぇ。ホントっすよぉ。
english: Let's say that even if I talk like this, you gotta believe I'm your friend. I swear, really.

japanese: 私ゼクシィっていうの。よろしくね。
english: I am Zexy. Nice to meet you.

japanese: 戦いは力だけじゃダメ。頭を使わなくちゃね。
english: Strength isn't all. You have to use your head sometimes in a fight, too.

japanese: この塔の中、モンスターさえいなければいいデートスポットになるのにね。残念だわ！
english: Ah, if only there weren't those monsters, this tower would make such a fancy spot for dates! What a shame!

japanese: 塔に挑む男達ってろくでなしばっかり！
english: All those men going into the tower are just good-for-nothings!

japanese: もう皆して塔塔って！　塔に何があるって言うのよ！
english: All they can talk about is the tower, the tower! Why do they care so much about that tower?!

japanese: 頭にくるわよね！　あの男ったら私より回復薬の方が大事だっていうのよ！
english: It blows, right?! They care more about my medicines than about me, or what?!

japanese: この前のお客ったら５０階のモンスター倒したってのに勇者の証取らなかったっていうのよ！
english: I got a customer who went to the 50th floor and killed the monster, and told me he still didn't get the Emblem of the Hero!

japanese: 酒場であった酔っぱらいが塔からいきなり放り出されたって悔しがってたわ！
english: There was this drunkard at the bar that was whining about being suddenly thrown out of the tower!

japanese: 塔に地下があるって噂、聞いた事ある？　信じちゃだめよ。１００％嘘だから。
english: There is a rumor that the tower has a basement, but don't you believe that! That's pure lies!

japanese: 世界中を旅してるって男に聞いたの。塔があるのはここだけじゃないらしいの！
english: A man traveling the world told me that this tower isn't the only one!

japanese: 私、今日はすっごく機嫌悪いの！なんか文句あるの！
english: I am so pissed today! What's your problem?!

japanese: 私は神様なんて信じない！　だってさわれもしないし、私には男がそばに居る方がいいわ！
english: I don't believe in no god! What's his deal if you can't come in contact with him? I'd rather have my man by my side!

japanese: 「勇者の証」って手に入れるとどうなるのかしらね？
english: I wonder what happens when you get your hands on the Emblem of the Hero.

japanese: この塔ってどのくらいの高さなのかしら？　考えた事無い？
english: Blast this tower, how high does it even go? What? You never asked that yourself?

japanese: 私、鏡の粉が欲しいの。そしたらこのピアス、メッキできるのになぁ。
english: I'd love to get mirror powder. Oh, how I would put it on those earrings!

japanese: アイスシールドってきれいなんだってね。一度見てみたいわ。
english: They say the ice shield is super pretty. Woah, I hope I can see one someday.

japanese: 私ってかなりかわいいわよね。なのに男達は皆、私をおいて塔にいっちゃうの。
english: Yeah, I'm cute, I know. Why are all the men leaving me alone to go in that tower then?

japanese: 私の名はマハーノレ。そなたが戦士の家系なら私と話してもあまり意味はないかもしれん。
english: My name is Mahanole. If war is your trade, you probably won't have much to gain from addressing me.

japanese: 魔法使いの家系の者は体力と腕力が低い。薬を活用せねば苦労するだろう。
english: Those of magician lineage are weak in body. They must know how to use potions, for their own good.

japanese: ヒールとは相手の体力をほんの少し奪い、それを増幅して自分の体力にする魔法だ。
english: The heal magic steals a tiny bit of the target's health to restore your own.

japanese: 魔法は神に最も近い力。魔法力を無駄使いするものは神の力を無駄使いしているという事だ。
english: Magic is the force closest to God. Wasting magic is wasting the power of God.

japanese: モンスターには属性を持つ者もいる。その属性の魔法で攻撃してもダメージは与えられない。
english: Monsters do have elemental traits. Attacking them with magic sharing their element won't damage them.

japanese: 敵の属性を見切る事が大切だ。
english: It is very important to learn the elemental traits of your enemies.

japanese: モンスターによっては魔法を使う隙がないかもしれん。その時は己の腕力だけが頼りになる。
english: Some monsters will probably not let you have the luxury of casting magic. At such times, you can only trust int the strength of your arms.

japanese: 魔法使いの家系の者として、魔法回復薬は常に持ち歩くべきだろう
english: As a descendant of magician lineage, you should always carry magic restoring potions with you.

japanese: 魔法使いだからとて体は鍛えねばならん。
english: Even though you are a magician, you need to train your body.

japanese: 攻撃魔法はフレア、アイス、エレキの順に覚える。
english: You will learn the magic of flare, ice and shock, in that order.

japanese: 回復魔法はヒールとハイヒールの２つだ。だがハイヒールはそう簡単には覚える事は出来ん。
english: There are two rejuvenating magics: heal and high heal. But learning high heal is no easy feat.

japanese: 剣の魔法を知っているか？　敵の弱点属性の魔法剣ならば２倍のダメージを与えられるのだ。
english: Do you know of the magic of the sword? A sword enchanted with the element the monster is weak to will inflict twice the damage.

japanese: 魔法剣は知力によって使える時間が異なるのだ。
english: Intelligence affects magic weapons; the higher it is, the longer they last.

japanese: 知力の低い魔法使いは腕力のない戦士と同じ、役立たずだ。
english: A magician with dim wits is as useless as a weak warrior.

japanese: 人型のモンスターは魔法を使うものが多い。気を付けるがよい。
english: Many humanoid monsters make use of magic. Be wary.

japanese: 魔法を３種類とも使うモンスターがいるそうだ。ジギーもそいつだけには会いたくないらしい。
english: There appears to be a monster who can use all three magic elements. I think Ziggy doesn't ever want to cross its path again.

japanese: ボーナスポイントを割り振って
総ての入力が終了しました。
